To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
functional richness is lost in benthic communities exposed to ocean warming and acidification and that functional loss occurs more rapidly than taxonomic loss.

(1) functional diversity of benthic marine organisms decreases along natural gradients in CO2 concentration, (2) functional loss is greater than the loss of species diversity, (3) the functional richness of the community is not buffered by the functional redundancy of individual species.
“The functional diversity of benthic marine assemblages exposed to ocean acidifica- tion is greatly reduced, resulting in a loss of functional redundancy.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of ocean acidification (decreasing seawater pH) on the biodiversity and functioning of marine ecosystems.
the effects of environmental change (i.e., ocean acidification) on marine biodiversity.
the effects of environmental change (e.g. ocean acidification) on biodiversity and the consequences of shifts of species composition for marine ecosystems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the loss of functional biodiversity is greater than the loss of taxonomic biodiversity.
the functional loss of benthic marine community is greater than the loss in taxonomic diversity along the CO2 gradient.
“Functional richness is reduced in acidified communities, and functional loss is more marked than the corresponding taxonomic diversity loss”.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the loss of functional richness in benthic communities exposed to acidified conditions is greater than that of taxonomic richness.
functional diversity is lost under acidified conditions, and that functional redundancy is low.

functional diversity is not buffered by redundancy under acidification, even in highly diversified assemblages, and that the loss of functional richness under acidification is more pronounced than taxonomic diversity loss.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the loss of species diversity under ocean acidification is not compensated by an increase in functional redundancy, and that the range of functional traits is greatly reduced in acidified conditions.
ocean acidification can cause a reduction of functional diversity in benthic communities.
the loss of biodiversity due to ocean acidification will likely affect ecosystem functioning, and that this loss will be greater than expected based on taxonomic diversity alone.
